conflicts: A(z7P4 -> a5D4, 715 nm): Paladugu et al. 2025 measure 1.15(20)e3 s^-1 from MOT loss; NIST ASD / Whaling & Brault 1988 give 6(2)e5 s^-1 (500 times larger; Whaling & Brault themselves flag self-absorption problems for the z7P branching fractions) and Palmeri & Wyart theory 4e4 s^-1. The MOT value is kept.

Isotope shifts of the 379.8 nm line: Paladugu et al. 2025 vs Aufmuth et al. 1978 differ by more than 2 sigma for 92-96 (920.4(1.9) vs 899(3) MHz) and 100-96 (-812.0(1.9) vs -803(1) MHz); Aufmuth uncertainties are statistical only. Paladugu values kept.

z7P lifetimes: Kwiatkowski et al. 1981 (16.3(8), 15.8(8), 14.7(7) ns for J = 2, 3, 4) vs Duquette et al. 1981 (17.1, 17.0, 15.9 ns, +-5 %) vs Whaling et al. 1984 (z7P4: 14.5(4) ns, derived from the quoted decay rate). All agree within about 1.5 sigma; Kwiatkowski kept as entry because it was read directly.
Isotopic abundances: IAEA Live Chart values are used; the NIST Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions page lists slightly different numbers (e.g. 95Mo 15.84(11) %, 98Mo 24.39(37) %).
not_found: Lifetimes of the other 43 drawn odd levels (z5F, z5D, y5D, x5D, y5F, w5D, v5F, u5F, t5F, 3D/3F levels, numbered levels ...): measured for 56 levels by Whaling, Hannaford, Lowe, Biemont, Grevesse, JQSRT 32, 69 (1984) and for 14 levels (31654.79-47184.52 cm^-1) by Jiang et al., J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 30, 489 (2013), but both are paywalled (ScienceDirect / Optica refused access) and no open copy was located; only the abstracts were read. Hannaford & Lowe, Opt. Eng. 22(5) (1983) likewise not accessible.

Hyperfine constants A, B of 95Mo/97Mo in the metastable a5S2, a5D0-4 levels and in z7P2,3,4 and other odd levels: measured by Olsson et al., Phys. Scr. 29, 61 (1984) and 34, 24 (1986), Brenner et al., Z. Phys. A 316, 247 (1984) and Pendlebury & Ring, J. Phys. B 5 (doi:10.1088/0022-3700/5/2/035); the abstracts opened give no numbers and the full texts (IOP, Springer) were not accessible.

Isotope shifts in Mo I lines other than 379.8 nm (Aufmuth et al. 1978, 16 lines; Goble & Palmer, J. Phys. B 18, 2181 (1985); Olsson et al. 1986): full texts not accessible. The abstract of Aufmuth et al. gives only relative delta<r^2> values.
Measured Lande g factors beyond those already in the NIST levels file (Brenner et al. 1984 measured gJ of a5D, a5S, a5P, c5D by atomic-beam magnetic resonance): values not accessible.
Resonance-ionization schemes for Mo with wavelengths: the CERN RILIS database requires a login; no open paper giving a Mo scheme with level energies was located.

Measured branching fractions newer than Whaling & Brault 1988 (the NIST source) other than the two z7P4 leak rates above: none located. The full Whaling & Brault table is hosted at http://kurucz.harvard.edu/atoms/4200/whalingbrault.dat and is what NIST ASD already carries.

Second pass (Crossref, OSTI ETDEWEB, arXiv API, CORE, Wayback Machine, Kurucz atoms/4200): no open copy of Whaling et al. 1984 or Jiang et al. 2013 was found, so the 43 drawn odd levels without lifetime stay empty. The Kurucz directory holds only the Whaling & Brault 1988 branching/level tables (already the NIST source) and calculated lifetimes (life4200.dat, semi-empirical; not entered because measurements exist)

Hyperfine constants of the metastable a5S2 and a5D levels: Brenner, Buettgenbach, Glaeser, Kloster, Roeder, Rupprecht, Traeber, Z. Phys. A 316, 247 (1984) (abstract read on OSTI and via Wayback: A, B and g_J measured for a5D, a5S, a5P, c5D by ABMR, plus isotope shifts) and Dubke, Jitschin, Meisel, Childs, Phys. Lett. A 65, 109 (1978) (abstract: B factors of metastable levels, giving Q(95Mo) = -0.015(4) b, Q(97Mo) = +0.017(4) b, Q97/Q95 = -11.50(3)) print no level constants in their abstracts
notes: Lifetimes from Kwiatkowski 1981 and Duquette 1981 were read from the abstracts of the original papers (the abstracts list the numbers); the papers themselves are paywalled. Hyperfine constants of the ground state are the directly measured (uncorrected) ABMR values in MHz, B converted from kHz. Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second). Frequencies are for 98Mo (boson, no hyperfine structure). The 15 lifetime entries above 39000 cm^-1 are J >= 5 levels that the site does not draw yet; the Whaling-Chevako-Lawler numbers were read from an OCR text layer of the scanned paper and checked by eye for the obvious OCR slips (e.g. "t4.0" = 14.0). Second pass: no new numerical entries could be sourced for Mo; see not_found for what was tried.
